memory_candidates.content: When validate-state.sh (or any hand-rolled bash+jq validator in this repo) hard-FAILs on an unknown field that turns out to carry live, non-null consumer data, check for a markdown-embedded writer before concluding 'no writer found'. In this codebase, commands and skills are markdown files whose literal jq/bash snippets ARE the executable write path (e.g. /review's active_goal write in commands/review.md, /spawn's previous_status write in skills/skill-spawn/SKILL.md) -- a grep scoped to *.sh alone will miss these and produce a false 'orphaned field' conclusion.

For a hand-maintained schema/validator pair with no drift test (e.g. state-schema.json's property keys vs validate-state.sh's KNOWN_TOP_LEVEL_FIELDS/KNOWN_ENTRY_FIELDS arrays), the safe migration pattern when moving a hard-FAIL check to advisory-first is: (1) widen the schema and validator array together in one commit, (2) separately change the check's severity from log_fail to log_warn with a written PROMOTION CRITERION naming the concrete bar to re-promote, (3) add a schema-to-validator drift test modelled on test-status-vocabulary.sh's existing enum drift assertion, sanity-checked by temporarily removing one known-field name and confirming the test fails and names it. This sequencing let the ruling be ADDITIVE and testable at each step rather than a single large unverifiable edit.
